 Vice City and Port Gellhorn feature three strip clubs in Grand Theft Auto VI , giving players access to private dance experiences through the game's entertainment venues. According to a guide published by Beebom on November 19, 2026, the locations include NINE1NINE, Jack of Hearts, and Delights Cabaret. Two establishments operate in Vice City, while the third is located in Port Gellhorn.
 Each venue offers private dances for $300, although the available interactions do not extend to sexual intercourse. NINE1NINE sits south of Crosstown in Vice City. Jack of Hearts is positioned north of the same district, while Delights Cabaret serves players visiting Port Gellhorn.

 Players can locate the establishments through blue icons on the in-game map. Beebom's guide recommends selecting the appropriate marker, setting a waypoint, and traveling to the destination before entering the venue.

 Accessing the establishments also involves leaving the vehicle and entering on foot with weapons stored away. Inside, players can approach a dancer and use the L2 or LT button to look at her. Holding Triangle or Y briefly then brings up the option to request a private dance, which costs $300.
 Once the payment is made, the dancer guides the player character to a private VIP area. Players can sit there and watch the performance. Beebom also reports that players can offer additional $50 tips during a private dance. These payments allow dancers to extend their performances in the VIP areas.
 Despite these interactions, GTA 6 does not include sexual intercourse with strip club dancers. Rockstar Games has explicitly stated that the game does not feature prostitutes, citing the relationship system involving its protagonists, Jason and Lucia. Consequently, private dances and additional tipping represent the extent of the available interactions with dancers inside the three establishments. Players seeking romantic interactions with other characters instead have the relationship system involving Jason and Lucia, as well as the character Mandy.
